subject: Context length & token volume — pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@acmeai.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmeai.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Context length & token volume — pricing follow-up

Thanks again for the call today — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps so we can produce a tight pricing estimate: 

Recap (from our discovery):
- Primary workloads: customer-facing assistant (real-time chat) + periodic long-document summarization for enterprise customers.
- Typical session mix: ~70% real-time assistant, ~20% document summarization, ~10% long-batch/legal/archival summaries that look at very long contexts.
- Key ask: unit economics target (target $ / 1M tokens), and a clear sense of average prompt vs completion tokens so we can model cost at 8k/32k/128k context sizes.

Can you confirm the following usage/profile items and attach a couple of representative documents (for the 32k/128k workflows) so we can run a quick cost profile? I attached a small context_profile_template.csv you can fill or paste below. Specifics we need: 
- Monthly token volume (projected)
- Avg prompt tokens (per request) and avg completion tokens (per request), by workload if possible
- Percent of requests that need 8k vs 32k vs 128k contexts
- Any SLOs for latency / percent that must stay under X ms (helps advise dedicated vs hosted)

Proposed next steps:
1) You fill the template or paste numbers in a reply (should take <10 minutes).
2) We run a 50–200 doc profiling job against sample documents and return a short cost scenarios deck.
3) If numbers look good, we propose a pilot (trial credits + streaming SLA) and a pricing tranche aligned to your target unit economics.

Attaching: context_profile_template.csv (blank), will also send a quick estimate once we get the numbers.

Thanks — happy to hop on another 20–30m if helpful.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0191
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@acmeai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmeai.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Context length & token volume — pricing follow-up

Hi Marissa — thanks, nice to meet you all. Below are the numbers from our side (pulled from product analytics + a small sample export). I also attached a short usage snapshot (acme_usage_snapshot.pdf) and filled your template. Let me know if anything needs clarification.

High-level current/projection (monthly):
- Projected active users: 120k MAU (end of Q2 target)
- Projected monthly calls: ~1.8M user requests (mix below)
- Projected monthly tokens (approx): prompt tokens = 32M, completion tokens = 96M (total ~128M tokens/month)

Avg tokens by workload (sampled):
1) Real-time assistant (70% of calls)
   - Avg prompt tokens: 280
   - Avg completion tokens: 600
   - Typical context needed: ≤8k most of the time
2) Document summarization (20% of calls)
   - Avg prompt tokens: 6,200 (we send the doc + user instruction)
   - Avg completion tokens: 1,800 (condensed summary)
   - Typical context needed: ~32k for full-doc summarization (we chunk transcriptions into a single request when possible)
3) Long-archival / legal deep-dive (10% of calls)
   - Avg prompt tokens: 28,000
   - Avg completion tokens: 12,000
   - Typical context needed: 128k occasionally (we may stream in pages, but want whole-doc semantics)

Distribution of context-length needs: ~80% 8k, ~15% 32k, ~5% 128k (when we run deep-dive workflows).

Budget / target unit economics:
- Current procurement guidance: budget of $15k–$35k/month for inference (targeting cost per 1M tokens between $20–$30 to be competitive with our current vendor).
- If you can show $/1M tokens closer to $20 with comparable latency and quality we’d be very interested in trialing.

Let us know if you want a small set of sample docs for the 32k/128k cases — I can drop them in the Drive link.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of ML Ops, Acme AI
samantha@acmeai.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@acmeai.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Context length & token volume — pricing follow-up

Samantha — this is fantastic, thanks for the data. I pulled a quick back-of-envelope to align expectations and outline a low-friction next step.

Back-of-envelope (very rough) using Redwood hosted list-price assumptions and workload mix you provided:
- Total tokens/month (your projection): ~128M tokens
- Weighted avg tokens per request ~ (0.7*(280+600) + 0.2*(6200+1800) + 0.1*(28000+12000)) / 1 = ~3,360 tokens/request (note: illustrative)

Scenarios (ballpark):
- If target is $20 / 1M tokens => monthly bill ~ $2,560 (for 128M tokens) — however, this ignores context-length multiplier effects (32k/128k models are materially more expensive per token and may increase GPU-run time).
- With 15% 32k and 5% 128k usage, realistic estimate for equivalent quality/perf could land in the $6k–$20k/month range depending on model family and quantization/latency requirements.

What we recommend next:
1) Run a 50-doc profiling job on your representative 32k/128k docs (we'll measure tokens, tokenization inefficiencies, and wall-clock for a few representative model variants). Can you drop 30–50 sample docs in the Drive folder linked below?
2) We will return a 2-page cost scenarios deck with: expected monthly cost per model variant, latency/throughput tradeoffs, and a suggested pilot configuration (hosted vs dedicated).
3) If the numbers align with your $/1M target, we propose a 60-day pilot: (a) 50k token trial credits, (b) priority onboarding, and (c) a term-sheet with a target $/1M token price for committed volume.

I attached an initial estimate (redwood_pricing_estimate_v1.pdf) with model-variant comparisons and assumptions. The HubSpot deal is updated: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-12345.

If that plan looks good I’ll schedule the profiling run and propose a quick 30m tech sync next week to walk the team through the sample ingestion.

—Marissa

Quick note from product direction: if Acme’s 128k needs and throughput projections are sustained, we should explore Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) early — it gives better unit economics at scale and predictable latency. Happy to run TCO (dedicated vs hosted) as part of the profile deliverable.

Jordan Blake
Head of Platform Growth, Redwood Inference
